Subject: Question on invoice splitting / proration and tax liability for order form

Hi Jordan,

Quick one as we review the order form with our finance team: we need clarity on three operational items before we route a PO:

1) Invoice splitting / proration: Helios will pre-pay a portion of the annual commit as an upfront credit. How does Redwood handle proration if we add seats mid-quarter or reduce consumption in Q2? We want the invoice to reflect prorated credits rather than an automatic credit adjustment on the next invoice.

2) Tax / VAT liability: Helios operates in the US and EU. For EU spend where VAT may apply, will Redwood issue a VAT invoice (we prefer that) or do you expect customers to self-assess? If Redwood issues VAT invoices, we need the vendor tax ID and the exact invoicing entity.

3) Payment milestones & net terms: For the upfront credit we typically need a single invoice for the committed amount, then monthly usage invoices. Can you confirm Redwood's recommended milestone schedule (e.g., upfront invoice then monthly usage with net30)?

Attaching our internal PO template to show routing. Can you loop in legal/finance on your side so we can get a final redline?

Thanks,
Emily Santos
Head of Procurement, Helios Health

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear list, this is helpful. High level answers below; I'll route to legal/finance for firm language and an updated order form redline.

1) Proration / credits: We can do prorated credit application on the invoice itself (preferred) — i.e., the upfront credit will be consumed against monthly usage with a prorated line item. If seats change mid-month we calculate prorata days on active seats. We'll put the formula in the order form appendix so accountants can reconcile.

2) VAT / tax: Typically Redwood issues VAT invoices when we have VAT registration in the customer's country; otherwise customers self-assess. I don't want to guess here — looping Kimberly (legal) and Ben (rev ops) to confirm the invoicing entity and vendor tax ID and whether Helios can get a Redwood VAT invoice for EU-bound charges.

3) Milestones & net terms: Standard approach is upfront invoice for the committed amount (Net30) and then monthly usage invoices (Net30). If Helios needs Net45 we can discuss — that typically requires Finance approval tied to credit checks.

Next step: Kimberly / Ben — can you review and produce a short redline (order form + suggested tax clause) so Emily has something to circulate to her finance team? I attached the current order form with our internal comments.

Thanks for the ping — see legal's initial guidance below. I've also attached a draft clause you can share with Helios to minimize back-and-forth.

1) Invoicing entity & VAT: Redwood will issue VAT invoices where we are VAT-registered in the jurisdiction where the supply is deemed to occur. For the EU charges we expect to issue a VAT invoice if Helios suggests that EU-registered entity is the billing recipient. If Helios requests Redwood to issue VAT invoices for EU spend, we will need the customer's VAT number and invoicing entity for our VAT registrations. Language to propose: "Redwood shall invoice all amounts hereunder and, where applicable, will issue VAT invoices. Customer is responsible for providing any tax registration numbers required for issuance of VAT invoices. Except as required by law, taxes (including VAT) are the responsibility of the Customer."

2) Proration / credits: Recommend including an appendix with a deterministic proration formula: "Proration = (Daily rate) x (Number of days in billing period during which seat(s) were active) / (Total days in billing period)". We should also add an express line that upfront credits are reflected on the next invoice as a dedicated line item and will not be netted off historical invoices without a reconciliation.

3) Payment terms: Default to Net30 for both upfront and usage invoices. If Helios needs Net45, Finance approval is required and we'll track in the deal. Also suggest adding a payment milestone table in the order form: 1) Upfront commit invoice due within 30 days of signature; 2) Monthly usage invoices due within 30 days of invoice date.

4) PO & remittance: ask Helios to reference Redwood Order ID in the PO and include the billing contact and remit-to entity.
